# Repairing a dry-stone wall

A dry-stone wall holds together through weight and friction alone, so repairs start by taking down the failed section to sound footings. Sort the stone by size: foundation stones, through-stones, hearting and copestones.

Lay each course so that every stone covers the joint beneath it, one over two and two over one. Pack the hearting tight; loose hearting is the main cause of a belly in the finished face. Bind the two faces together with a through-stone about every metre.

Finish with copestones set on edge, each leaning slightly against its neighbour, so that wind and sheep cannot lift them. A good repair should be indistinguishable from the old work within a few winters.
